neighbours.label: A space directly followed by a character the tokenizer splits into raw byte pieces: uncommon emoji and symbols (chess pieces, snowman, APL), rare Chinese characters, many Korean syllables and katakana; also the long mark ー before a split katakana, and accented letters inside pointed Hebrew or polytonic Greek. Quiet when the same symbol is glued to a Latin word or punctuation, at text start, and for common characters kept as whole tokens (€, →, everyday Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic, accented Latin).
neighbours.short: space before a byte-split rare character
neighbours.notes: Step-out feeder of L32/N4095+ (play step hit CUDA OOM on stream, so the feeder was chosen as the top of the resident attribution ranking; no ablation drop measured, so no edge is recorded). Card: peak tokens are space+lead-byte pieces and 'ー'+lead byte; output suppresses continuation byte tokens on the + side (the - pole promotes them). Probes: spaced ♛ ☃ 🦎 纩 0.5-0.6, glued or quoted twins 0; common Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic, € and café 0; pointed Hebrew and polytonic Greek fire mid-word ~0.5. Solver leak (an Arabic corpus line with shadda, 0.80) did not replicate in a fresh shadda sentence (0). Test sentences written blind by a second author from the label only.
